On 1,065 synthetic, LLM-labelled items, grouping by question type and option count gives a bucket-macro ECE of 0.143, which a cross-fitted temperature per bucket reduces to 0.073. A single global temperature makes calibration worse, and the findings apply only to these checkpoints and this data.

entry.title: ReA-Bench: A benchmark for auditing whether AI agents behave responsibly
entry.summary: ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces ReA-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for auditing the behavior of autonomous agents. It organizes auditing challenges into six tiers, including internal safety knowledge, contradictions within trajectories, and missing information. The benchmark includes benign cases that resemble risky actions but are authorized and consistent with the task. Most samples come from real production trajectories, with paired versions to test auditor reliability.

entry.title: Time and Space: An evidence-grounded context framework for personal AI agents
entry.summary: Time and Space: A Dual-Axis, Evidence-Grounded Context Substrate for Personal Agents arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper argues that personal agents are limited by how context is represented rather than by model capacity. It proposes spatio-temporal context (STC), organized along a temporal axis and a relational semantic space, with every relation anchored to immutable source records. The authors formalise six invariants, a context operator, conflict detection, and a four-regime consumption taxonomy. They report measurements from a local SQLite-based retrieval prototype over 341 documents.

entry.title: HeMeR: reusing cached model states to keep robot agents' mixed memories efficient
entry.summary: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse arXiv · Nov 12, 2026HeMeR is an inference framework for embodied agents that combines declarative, procedural, and working memory. It keeps key-value states for memory contents that have not changed and recomputes only those affected by updates. In real-world robotic deployments, it reports 83.20% task success and cuts per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL.

entry.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended): A Local Test Kit for Small Coding Agents and Its Full Experiment Record
entry.summary: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper presents drydock-eval, a local evaluation kit for the small coding agent Gemma 4 E4B, with a container-isolated runner that passed 200 scripted escape tests, eight checks aligning the local setup with the hosted scorer, and paired statistics that respect repository clusters. It publicly releases the full record of its experiments, including 9,660 agent runs and 2,494 grading controls. Three prompt-driven agent changes that looked better on screening tasks were not confirmed on new tasks. Prompts and agent bundles are withheld.

entry.title: One Model, Two Precisions: Can Quantized Copies Disagree to Flag Small Model Errors?
entry.summary: One Model, Two Precisions: Does Disagreement Between Quantized Copies Tell You When a Small Model Is Wrong? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper asks whether disagreement between an 8-bit and a lower-precision quantized copy of the same model can serve as a per-question error score for abstention, escalation, or re-asking. The authors test Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B on 8,398 multiple-choice questions from ARC, MMLU and HellaSwag subsets. They find the disagreement score adds little over entropy, and that comparable gains appear with Gaussian weight noise, suggesting the signal is not specific to quantization.

entry.title: Where a one-pass decision model looks in long inputs
entry.summary: Where in the Input Does a One-Pass Decision Encoder Look? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies Laya, a small model that answers multiple-choice questions about a text in one pass within a 512-token window. Using 177 items, five tasks, three checkpoints and 93,275 scored requests, the authors show that when the evidence falls beyond the window, accuracy drops to about 26.4%, near chance. Model confidence does not reliably separate cut requests from read ones.

entry.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough: A Look at Turn-Taking Failures in Social Robots
entry.summary: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This short paper reviews earlier methods for improving speech recognition and turn-taking in interactions with social robots. It notes that speech recognition has improved considerably, but turn-taking failures and other misunderstandings remain too frequent. The authors argue that multimodal bidirectional streaming is needed to reduce how often turn-taking failures occur.

entry.title: How should planning agents reshape their search space when users revise requests?
entry.summary: How Should Planning Agents ReSHAPE Their Search Space? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Planning agents and benchmarks usually treat a user's initial request as fixed, even though users often discover acceptable trade-offs only after seeing options. The paper formalizes this as the ReSHAPE task, judging a revised request by whether its search space contains acceptable plans and a planner can find one. Analyzing 5,800 agent-revised specifications in travel and shopping, the authors find that one correct trade-off can raise a planner's success rate up to 4.6 times. Current agents admit at most 32% of acceptable plans, and showing concrete plans to users improves results over asking about preferences.

entry.title: From State of the Art to Human Prediction Algorithms: Comparing Interactive Art and Human Trajectory Prediction
entry.summary: From State of THE ART to Human Prediction Algorithms arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines human trajectory prediction algorithms, noting that as quantitative performance improves, consideration of human behavior, future intentions, and social interaction tends to decline. Using interactive art and prediction algorithms as examples, the authors analyze their structural and developmental commonalities through perception, interaction, and timing. They also report that some art-inspired prediction algorithms can derive intriguing patterns of human behavior from data.

entry.title: Scalable random features for hyperbolic latent variable models
entry.summary: Helgason-Fourier Random Features for Scalable Hyperbolic Latent Variables arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces Random Helgason-Fourier Features (RHFF), an explicit finite-dimensional feature map for kernels on hyperbolic space. It characterizes the spectral density used to draw RHFF frequencies, so kernels such as the Matérn family can be specified in the frequency domain, and proves a uniform approximation error bound. Building on this, the authors develop RHFF-LVM, a hyperbolic latent variable model that needs no quadrature, variational bounds or auxiliary variables, and report that it recovers a synthetic tree's metric more faithfully than all baselines and fits 5×10^5 points in 505 seconds.

entry.title: Fine-tuned small language model that generates synthetic clinical data to improve vital-sign prediction
entry.summary: Fine-Tuned Small Language Model for Synthetic Clinical Data Generation and Predictive Healthcare Analytics arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a clinical data augmentation method that uses a fine-tuned Microsoft Phi-2 small language model to generate synthetic samples. The model was adapted to the medical domain using QLoRA-based supervised fine-tuning on the MedQuad dataset and few-shot prompting. When the generated data augmented a small vital-sign dataset, an LSTM predictive model's classification accuracy rose from 89.0% to 93.7%, with consistent gains in precision, recall, and F1-score.

entry.title: Rational alignment of superintelligences through debate
entry.summary: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies a setup where superintelligent AI agents assist humans in question answering, knowing the correct answer while the human does not. It gives example mechanisms that control how the agent and human principal interact, without changing the agent's utility. It shows that a debate framework in which agents reason and act in a subgame perfect equilibrium yields more predictable outcomes and is sometimes favorable.

entry.title: Can vision-language models spot video event boundaries the way humans do?
entry.summary: Can an LVLM Perceive Event Boundaries Like a Human? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines whether Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) perceive event boundaries in videos consistently with humans. On the Kinetics-GEBD dataset, LVLMs refine candidate boundaries proposed by an unsupervised discovery method, achieving state-of-the-art unsupervised performance. The approach is extended to hour-long egocentric video using coarse-to-fine discovery and localized LVLM judgments, and the authors build the EgoBoundary benchmark, on which representative existing methods degrade substantially.

entry.title: HIFC-IQA: Train-free cross-domain image quality assessment using dual-process cognition
entry.summary: HIFC-IQA: Train-Free Cross-Domain Image Quality Assessment via Dual-Process Cognition arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses the domain shift between synthetic distortions and real-world image degradations in no-reference image quality assessment. It proposes HIFC, a completely train-free framework inspired by human dual-process cognition, which uses asymmetric perceptual decomposition to separate semantic content from distortion-sensitive features. The final quality score combines a memory consensus branch that retrieves a stable Fuzzy Quality Centroid from a synthetic reference gallery with an intuitive branch that captures aesthetic polarization via zero-shot vision-language alignment. The authors report state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks, with a notable margin in the synthetic-to-authentic setting.

entry.title: A unified framework for training physical action models
entry.summary: A Recipe for Physical Action Model Training arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how choices about robot model capacity, demonstration budgets, data composition, representation, and optimization are connected through a common conditional-distribution target. It uses nested learning oracles for exact risk accounting, together with local information geometry, conditional mutual information, and empirical convergence, to derive training prescriptions. Numerical checks with known targets reveal capacity-data coupling and representation-induced mixture mismatch. An analysis of 206 public PushT trajectories evaluates fixed-feature information-design criteria without fitting a policy.

entry.title: FPSRG: First-person post-training and response grids for simulating diverse users
entry.summary: FPSRG: Heterogeneous User Simulation First-Person Post-Training and Multidimensional Semantic Response Grids arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how to build language-model configurations that simulate individuals with different characteristics, retrievable by multidimensional target scores. The method, First-Person Semantic Response Grids (FPSRG), first post-trains the model to answer as the participant, then refines dimension-specific control vectors using self-report and behavioral targets. Joint scores are measured with the model frozen and stored in a searchable catalog. Reported results include mean five-axis control span rising from 30.75 to 40.45 after refinement, and a five-level vector catalog covering 92.2% of fixed targets in the five-dimensional region.

entry.title: DesignTaste: a benchmark comparing AI-generated visual designs with award-winning works
entry.summary: DesignTaste: Benchmarking AI-Generator Visual Design Against Award-Wining Works arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces DesignTaste, a benchmark that compares images generated by text-to-image AI models with award-winning design works. It builds 403 design briefs from Beste Plakate 2025 poster works and ADC 2026 works across 20 categories, and a single model judge scores each output and award-winning work on five dimensions. Only ArtArk achieves a higher mean overall score than the award-winning works on each dataset, and all six models score lower in Creative Originality. The authors conclude that producing finished, visually appealing images does not mean a model can develop good design solutions.

entry.title: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving
entry.summary: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a data and training recipe for improving formal theorem-proving models. The authors synthesize a 33.7B-token mid-training corpus covering decomposition, search, self-verification, and revision, and introduce the daVinci-Prover harness, which lets models interact with a Lean verifier in an isolated workspace. Using it, they collect about 36K agent trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. The method improves on a matched Qwen3-8B SFT-only baseline by an average of 13.7 points across MiniF2F, FATE-M, and ProofNet, and performs strongly on the Qwen3.5 series.

entry.title: SoScale: Second-order scale search for 4-bit floating-point model compression
entry.summary: SoScale: Second-Order Scale Search for FP4 Quantization arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes SoScale, a method for choosing hardware-valid scale codes in hierarchical FP4 quantization of large language model weights. It searches scales using a Hessian-aware layer reconstruction objective and combines this with GPTQ-style error recovery, so scales are selected by their effect on layer outputs rather than element-wise error. The authors report that across Qwen3 models, SoScale consistently reduces downstream quantization degradation under MXFP4, NVFP4, and HiF4.

entry.title: RMIT-ADM+S's TREC 2026 RAG entry: research agents, retriever ablations, and open-weight replication
entry.summary: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper reports the RMIT-ADM+S team's participation in the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation track, using the ClimbMix corpus. The team submitted seven research-agent runs built on proprietary OpenAI and open-weight models. Pre-submission ablations found that writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion were the main factors affecting answer quality. In the official evaluation, six of seven runs exceeded the track median, and the best run, brief-hybrid, tied the track maximum for Batch-1 vital coverage. Human preferences differed from automated coverage measures across batches.

entry.title: PhysCapBench: A cross-domain benchmark for video captions that describe physical processes
entry.summary: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces PhysCapBench, a benchmark of 1,500 human-verified video sequences spanning third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It scores captions for accuracy and coverage across seven physical dimensions. Compared with metadata captions, physical captions reduce video reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos. Enriched training instructions also improve benchmark scores and manipulation-policy success.

entry.title: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on One GPU
entry.summary: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents BlinkMimic, a method that speeds up training of whole-body motion tracking policies for humanoid robots. On a simulated Unitree G1, it trains one policy for all 40 LAFAN1 motion clips in 3.4 minutes on a single RTX 4090, measured until three consecutive checkpoints reach a normalized return of at least 0.82 with no failed clip (mean of three seeds). A leave-one-out ablation with three seeds per component shows which part of the training time each component affects.

entry.title: Predicting a Robot Operator's Layered Intent from Video of Teleoperation
entry.summary: I See What You Want: Decoding Hierarchical Operator Intent from Visual Teleoperation History arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines whether vision-language models can infer, from a short visual history of robot teleoperation, both the atomic action a human is performing and the broader mission it serves. The authors introduce VIAMO, a dataset of 6,600 episodes, and fine-tune a model called VIM on it. VIM outperforms GPT-4o and GPT-5.6 Luna on both action and mission prediction, and its predicted mission lets a vision-language-action policy take over from the operator in a real-world setting.

entry.title: Distilling image-text datasets so they generalize across model training stages
entry.summary: Model Distribution-Aware Multimodal Dataset Distillation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies multimodal dataset distillation, which compresses image-text data into a small synthetic set to cut the cost of vision-language pre-training. It proposes MDA-DD, which uses supervision from a dynamic staggered queue of models at different training stages, along with asymmetric dual projection and an uncentered second-order moment objective. Experiments on Flickr30K and MS-COCO report consistent retrieval improvements over existing methods across synthetic-data budgets.

entry.title: VBot Exo2Ego Policy: Lightweight Data Collection and Third-to-First-Person Video Generation
entry.summary: VBot Exo2Ego Policy: Lightweight Data Collection and Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents VBot Exo2Ego Policy, a video generation model that converts third-person videos into first-person views of a selected actor, aiming to expand first-person operation data from real-world footage. It also introduces a lightweight mobile app and data collection pipeline that record first- and third-person views synchronously along with camera geometry. The model builds on a pretrained video diffusion transformer, using geometric guidance and auxiliary supervision from semantic masks and hand keypoints, and it runs inference without target-camera calibration.

entry.title: Small Language Models for Routing LLM Capabilities: How Model Size and Prompt Tuning Affect Quality and Efficiency
entry.summary: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies using small language models to decide which optional capabilities, such as reasoning, retrieval, web search, and tool use, a large language model should activate for each query. The authors compare Qwen2.5 routers from 1.5B to 14B parameters under five prompting strategies, evaluating downstream answers on 127 questions with a fixed GPT-OSS-120B model. They find that higher router capacity does not consistently improve classification, and similar F1 scores can lead to different downstream results. The 14B router keeps answer quality close to enabling all capabilities while substantially reducing downstream token use and median latency, excluding router overhead.

entry.title: RICapBench: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Vision-Language Understanding of Remote Sensing Images
entry.summary: RICapBench: A Fine-Grained Visual Understanding Benchmark Dataset for Vision-Language Models in Remote Sensing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces RICapBench, a dataset and benchmark that combines instance localization with fine-grained captioning for remote sensing imagery. It contains 245,466 instance-level annotations and 498,005 spatial relation tuples across general, UAV, and dense small-object scenarios. The authors also propose the RelCap-F1 metric and a composite RICScore for evaluation. Testing 15 vision-language models, they find instance localization to be a major bottleneck, with LocateAnything achieving the highest RICScore of 31.68.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning that passes experience to future agent runs
entry.summary: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper notes that training LLM agents with scalar rewards discards fine-grained environment feedback such as error logs. The authors fix the Agentic Context Engineering harness and train one model to act, reflect, and curate task-specific playbooks. Each experience-handoff artifact is scored by its effect on future actor rollouts, and the role behaviors are optimized together. The method reports higher held-out performance than baselines across agentic benchmarks.

entry.title: Gravity and Flight: a method teaching AI models to reason about fine details in satellite imagery
entry.summary: Gravity and Flight: Learning to Navigate Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Scenes arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes Gravity and Flight (G&F), a framework that adapts vision-language models to remote sensing scenes using limited supervision. It combines Evidence-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning (EoT-SFT) with Relational Transfer Policy Optimization (RTPO), which verifies visual fidelity and evidence use across paired images. Using 1,008 demonstrations and 500 training pairs for harbor specialization, G&F achieves a mean score of 69.12 across six evaluation sets, outperforming the backbone and supervised initialization. The authors also report gains when applying G&F to urban scenes.

entry.title: Teaching with Blinks: Fixing Student Error Copying in Fine-Grained Visual Distillation
entry.summary: Teach with Blinks: Breaking Linguistic Momentum in On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes BlinkOPD, an on-policy distillation method for improving fine-grained visual perception in multimodal large language models. Each token is processed by the teacher twice, once with eyes open and once with eyes closed, to counter the teacher following the student's erroneous prefixes. A first-glance gain further strengthens correction on rollouts that conflict with the teacher. The authors report state-of-the-art average results on six fine-grained benchmarks using only 500 training images, and zero-shot gains on ten held-out benchmarks.

entry.title: FuGIBench: Testing When Streaming Video Models Should Wait, Prepare, or Respond
entry.summary: FuGIBench: Evaluating Reliable Preparation in Streaming Video arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces FuGIBench, a benchmark for streaming video in which a model decides whether to wait, make reversible preparations, or respond. It contains 19,893 synthetic tool-assistance videos across ten tool tasks and three tracks: handover, ordinary activity, and cancelled need. A single primary score rewards sustained preparation and alignment with the response interval, and penalizes unnecessary activity when waiting is prescribed.

entry.title: Saidzoda-Kazakh-EmbeddingGemma-300M: A small Kazakh text-embedding model trained on one epoch of generated questions
entry.summary: Saidzoda-Kazakh-EmbeddingGemma-300M: How Far One Epoch of Generated Questions Takes a Small Kazakh Embedder arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper fine-tunes the small open embedder EmbeddingGemma-300M on Kazakh for one epoch, using 208,511 training pairs, mostly Kazakh questions generated by the authors' language model from encyclopedia, Wikipedia, news and book passages and checked by a second model. On the Kazakh Belebele retrieval test, recall@1 rises from 60.8% to 78.0% and recall@10 from 76.3% to 91.4%. The model is compared with other models that have published MTEB scores and with several Kazakh-specific embedders on the same test.

entry.title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated Vision-Language Model for Chest X-ray Report Writing
entry.summary: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents TransXplainRRG, a large vision-language model that automatically generates radiology reports from chest X-rays. It combines a Swin Transformer image encoder with a text encoder that incorporates patient medical history, and extracts only abnormal findings to refine reports. The model was trained on MIMIC-CXR and tested on the unseen IU X-Ray dataset, scoring 0.327 and 0.605 on the GREEN metric, both above MAIRA-2 under the same setting. A preliminary evaluation by radiologists on 100 generated reports was also conducted.

entry.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
entry.summary: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes CoMem, a query-guided framework that compresses long inputs selectively by learning memory representations conditioned on both the document and the query. It combines contrastive compressor learning, same-context hard negative mining, and bidirectional attention among memory slots. Experiments on question answering and RULER-NIAH benchmarks report that CoMem outperforms existing context compression methods across compression ratios.

entry.title: RADIANT: A Redundancy-Aware Method for Universal Multi-Modal Fusion
entry.summary: RADIANT: Redundancy-Aware Information Allocation for Universal Multi-Modal Fusion arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces RADIANT (Redundancy-Aware Dynamic Information Allocation Network), a task-general framework for fusing multiple data modalities. It organizes fusion around suppressing redundant cross-modal overlap, preserving modality-unique information, and composing task-conditioned synergy through cross-modal interaction. The method uses stable matrix-exponential projections to reduce interference between shared and unique streams, and a task memory with hard positive updates to choose which synergistic interactions to activate. The authors report consistent improvements across six heterogeneous fusion tasks, including raising downstream detection mAP@0.5 on FLIR from 91.2% to 96.8%.

entry.title: Governing Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
entry.summary: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework that controls when autonomous agents adopt changes they generate to their own prompts, memories, tools, and policies. It separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, tests frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, and uses non-inferiority tests to protect declared capabilities. The authors give statistical bounds for adaptively generated candidates, cumulative degradation along reference lineages, and a Monte Carlo stress test of evaluator optimism. The guarantees depend on bounded scores, fresh sampling and declared distributions, and do not establish general agent safety.

entry.title: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: a persistent latent state that adapts pretrained language models over time
entry.summary: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: Persistent Latent-State Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes Recursive SALM, a framework in which a persistent latent state updated with each observation generates adaptations of a pretrained language model. Experiments with a frozen GPT-2 small show that on a four-turn hypothesis-inference task, a latent-gated LoRA using only a 64-dimensional state reaches 89.1% accuracy, close to the 88.0% of a full-context LoRA baseline. The authors conclude that persistent latent-conditioned adaptation can support sequential inference when earlier evidence is absent from the decoder context.

entry.title: CLIP adaptation for few-shot plant disease recognition using descriptions and local evidence
entry.summary: Description-Guided CLIP Adaptation with Local Evidence Calibration for Few-Shot Plant Disease Recognition arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a two-stage method that adapts the CLIP vision-language model for recognizing plant diseases from few labeled examples. It enriches class names with symptom and comparative descriptions, then uses these to calibrate global image-text matching with class-relevant image patch evidence. The encoders are first updated with lightweight parameters, then frozen while a linear classifier is trained, with text prototypes used for cross-domain prediction. Experiments on PlantVillage, Cassava, Pear, and PlantDoc report higher accuracy than compared methods in most settings.

entry.title: MutAtlas: a PDB-wide, energy-guided map of how protein mutations affect function
entry.summary: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper addresses the scarcity of experimentally measured protein mutation data by exhaustively enumerating single-site substitutions on experimentally resolved PDB structures. It aligns mutation signals from physics-based energy models, protein language models, and inverse folding models into a large augmentation dataset, showing that these models often disagree in their mutation distributions. The authors propose an unsupervised multi-source mutation preference distillation framework that models this disagreement without using experimental labels, and report the best overall performance among evaluated zero-shot baselines and naive fusion methods on ProteinGym. The dataset and evaluation pipeline are released.

entry.title: IsharaBART: An Efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation
entry.summary: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces IsharaBART, a bidirectional generative model for translating between gloss notation and sentences in Bangla Sign Language (BdSL). It is built on BART with denoising training objectives and was trained on a dataset of 1,000 annotated gloss-sentence pairs, expanded to 4,831 pairs through augmentation. Compared with four larger baseline models under identical conditions, it achieves comparable or better bidirectional performance while using fewer than 10% of their parameters.

entry.title: DIAGNO: A Spherical Neural Operator for Forecasting Uneven Earth Dynamics
entry.summary: DIAGNO: Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators for Heterogeneous Earth Dynamics Modeling arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces DIAGNO, a spherical neural operator for forecasting Earth system dynamics. Existing spherical neural operators rely on a rotation equivariance assumption that treats the Earth as a homogeneous system. DIAGNO drops this assumption, explicitly modeling interactions between spectral modes and using the diagonal structure of the spherical spectrum to capture zonal and meridional dynamics. Experiments on simulated fluid dynamics and atmosphere and ocean reanalysis data report state-of-the-art multi-step forecasting performance.

entry.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
entry.summary: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how a node's structural role relates to its radius in hyperbolic embeddings, finding that bridge nodes sit closer to the center in ordinary graphs but not consistently in hypergraphs. It proposes HyBridge, a self-supervised framework that estimates bridge scores using the external connectivity of hyperedges, positions nodes radially according to these scores, and applies contrastive learning to keep nodes distinguishable. Experiments on 10 real-world hypergraphs show it outperforms 22 competing methods, with node classification gains of up to 9.82%.

entry.title: DRAMA: Speeding Up Multimodal Diffusion Language Models by Analyzing Attention Redundancy
entry.summary: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses the slow inference of multimodal diffusion large language models, which process long sequences dominated by visual tokens over many denoising steps. By measuring attention tensors across spatial and temporal axes, the authors find that attention concentrates on a sparse set of visual tokens and stabilizes quickly across denoising steps. They propose DRAMA, a training-free framework with spatial-redundancy-aware visual token pruning and sufficiency-guided adaptive stopping. The authors report an average 18.67 times inference speedup across six vision-language benchmarks while maintaining competitive accuracy.

entry.title: SUMNO: A Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
entry.summary: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces SUMNO, a neural operator for predicting fluid flow fields on regular grids, built by unrolling a multigrid V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network. It uses parameter-free up- and downsampling with additive skip connections, convolutions at finer resolutions, and shifted-window attention at the coarsest level. On four unsteady and steady flow benchmarks against five baselines, SUMNO is reported to be best in 5 of 7 settings and second in the other two. The authors state it cuts 10-step rollout MSE by about 30% versus the strongest baseline while using 9.4 million parameters, fewer than three baselines exceeding 130 million.

entry.title: Reconstructing Hands from Silhouettes: Multi-View Hand Modeling Trained on Synthetic Data
entry.summary: Hand in Silhouette: Synthetic-to-Real Multi-View Hand Reconstruction via Binary Masks arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents SilHand, a calibrated multi-view hand reconstruction method that uses only binary hand masks, which can be obtained cheaply, to narrow the gap between synthetic and real images. It is trained on a large synthetic dataset of 46.8k grasping poses and 60k free-hand samples and tested on five real-world benchmarks. Using masks rendered from reference hands, relative reconstruction accuracy rises from 49.2% to 63.4%, and accuracy improves as the synthetic training set grows. Under mask corruption, reconstruction error increases by at most 1.63 mm.

entry.title: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the AI Era
entry.summary: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the Age of AI arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper argues that AI is rapidly expanding organizations' capacity to produce and analyze data, shifting data scientists' focus toward assessing findings' credibility and importance and judging when evidence generalizes across contexts. Based on a roundtable of academic researchers and industry practitioners, it examines three ways causal inference and experimentation practitioners can turn analytical capacity into better decisions. These are preserving the learning value of experiments beyond individual tests, combining experimental, observational, and synthetic evidence, and keeping evaluation in step with AI's evolving capabilities and uses.

entry.title: Does deep knowledge tracing learn meaning-based links between knowledge components?
entry.summary: Does Deep Knowledge Tracing Learn Semantic Relations Between Knowledge Components? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines whether relations between knowledge components (KCs) learned by Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) models are semantic. The authors build text-derived KC representations with nine pipelines and compare DKT-derived relation graphs with semantic similarity structures, finding only weak and inconsistent alignment. Adding semantic information to DKT did not consistently outperform the standard baseline. The authors conclude that DKT-derived relations are not primarily semantic, and that behavioral, temporal, structural, or psychometric signals may also shape them.

entry.title: Adaptive Mamba Network for Long-Term Climate Temperature Forecasting
entry.summary: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents Deep DualMamba, a deep learning framework for forecasting temperature over time, built on an enhanced version of the Mamba network with selective structured state space models. It uses an adaptive bidirectional Mamba encoder and a hardware-aware parallel recurrent algorithm, and it avoids attention and MLP layers, giving linear complexity with sequence length. The authors also provide a theoretical analysis of the model's approximation ability and convergence. The framework is applied to historical meteorological data from UK monitoring stations.

entry.title: Turning Large Language Models into Efficient Fast-Decision Models via Adaptive Computation
entry.summary: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how to convert large language models into fast decision-making models, which usually keeps the full backbone and swaps in a decision head, so every decision runs through all layers. The authors find decision information concentrates in middle layers and the final six layers can be removed without loss. They propose training a full model jointly with prefix sub-models that share its final layers and decision head, using a lightweight gate to decide whether extra computation is needed. Across seven decision benchmarks, the approach matches or outperforms independently trained models while offering better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

entry.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors: how language models weigh risk
entry.summary: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper evaluates how risk-averse or risk-tolerant large language models are across various contexts and task demands, and how stable and consistent their behavior is. It presents a toolkit for building model risk profiles that can predict behavior and be extended with new risk evaluations. The authors report that 2026 state-of-the-art models are more stable, consistent, and risk neutral than older models. They suggest these trends are related, since newer models more often use expected value maximization as a decision procedure.

entry.title: Wanda-guided sparse perturbations for faster forward-only fine-tuning of large language models
entry.summary: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes WIS-MeZO, which uses Wanda weight-activation saliency to build task-specific sparse perturbation masks while keeping the pretrained model dense. The authors analyze mask quality through gradient energy capture and relate it to gradient estimation and convergence. Across 16 benchmarks with LLaMA and Qwen models from 3B to 32B parameters, WIS-MeZO reports higher aggregate scores than MeZO and reaches comparable validation losses in fewer steps. Comparisons with random and magnitude-based sparse perturbations emphasize the value of selecting informative perturbation coordinates.

entry.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits Small Language Model Aggregation in Fermi Estimation
entry.summary: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper tests whether teams of small language models can reduce error on Fermi estimation questions by averaging their answers. Using 2.51 million answers from 15 open-weight models given before any communication, the authors split each answer's log10 error into a per-item component shared across a model's draws and a residual. They find the item-level component accounts for a median 0.906 of error variance, so teams of thirty reduce a single agent's error by a median of only 1.7%.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware diffusion for selective generative video deraining
entry.summary: Selective Generative Restoration for Video Deraining via Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses video deraining, where rain streaks and occlusions degrade frames unevenly across regions. The authors propose Selective Generative Restoration, which activates generative priors only where restoration uncertainty is high, and implement it as SGVD, a one-step diffusion framework. Region-level uncertainty is estimated from stochastic differences between two one-step diffusion predictions, and an anchor-guided trajectory consistency mechanism reduces temporal drift across frames. The authors report superior restoration quality, perceptual quality, and temporal consistency compared with state-of-the-art video deraining methods.

entry.title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully reproducible CALPHAD assessment from evidence to phase diagrams
entry.summary: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces ORCHID-SAGE, a standard that encodes the expert judgments behind thermodynamic database assessments (CALPHAD) into formal, reproducible and automatable protocols. In a first application to Cr-Ni, the database was regenerated from its record by a script, by an AI agent using the Model Context Protocol, and by a refit using only public sources, yielding the same predictions. The authors argue that databases recorded this way can be updated by AI agents as new evidence appears, while human experts retain the judgment and it remains documented.

entry.title: DEDCA: Test-Time Adaptation for Detecting AI-Generated Images from Unseen Generators
entry.summary: DEDCA: Test-Time Adaptation for Generalized AI-Generated Image Detection arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses the problem that AI-generated image detectors perform poorly on images from unseen generators. It proposes DEDCA, a framework combining CLIP-based semantic evidence with trace evidence from shuffled entropy and residual statistics, fused per sample by a reliability-aware gate. The disagreement between the two evidence streams serves as an unlabeled signal for adaptation to the target domain. The authors report 92.0% average accuracy on the GenImage benchmark.

entry.title: Fixing spurious correlations in conditional diffusion models by doubly robust target correction
entry.summary: Overcoming Spurious Correlations in Conditional Diffusion Models via Doubly Robust Target Correction arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Conditional diffusion models can memorize spurious correlations in their training data, causing outputs to drift from the intended target distribution. This paper proposes DR-Diff, a framework that efficiently fine-tunes pre-trained conditional diffusion models to adapt to the target distribution without retraining from scratch. The authors prove that DR-Diff reduces target risk at the population level and has a pseudo-doubly robust property. Experiments on synthetic datasets show noise prediction accuracy matching models trained from scratch, and reduced inter-group disparities in downstream classification.

entry.title: StateAlign: Reinforcement learning that teaches tool-using AI agents to decide based on task state
entry.summary: StateAlign: Internalizing State-Aware Decision-Making for Reliable Multi-Turn Tool Agents via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces StateAlign, which combines task-state construction with state-contrastive reinforcement learning to train language model agents for multi-turn tool use. The method pairs states with different action requirements and uses token-level contrasts to reward outputs that fit the current state. Across five base models, it improves results on BFCL v4 multi-turn, ToolSandbox, and When2Call. On Qwen3-8B, BFCL v4 multi-turn accuracy rises from 45.5% to 55.2%, and no-tool hallucination on SimpleToolHalluBench falls from 62.2% to 56.1% compared with outcome-only training.

entry.title: LoCoJAX: Host-local coordination for training small AI models with reinforcement learning on Google TPUs
entry.summary: LoCoJAX: Host-Local Coordination for Small-Model RL on TPUs arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how coordination overhead in reinforcement learning on TPUs changes with model size, finding host orchestration takes 36% of step time for a 0.6B model while network communication dominates for large models. It proposes LoCoJAX, which runs rollouts and reward processing locally on each TPU host while keeping global training synchronous. Compared with a tuned Pathways baseline on Qwen3-0.6B, its colocated mode is 1.3 to 3.6 times faster per step. A Ray-managed disaggregated mode helps only when rollout dominates the step and receives most of the hosts.

entry.title: SAGE-QA: A Semantic-Aware, Grounded Way to Score Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
entry.summary: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0 arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces SAGE-QA, an evaluation framework for closed-context question answering that combines reference-based Semantic Equivalence Scoring with passage-based Re-Validation Scoring. Tested on 10,000 SQuAD 2.0 validation examples, it compares zero-shot frontier models with open-weight models, untuned and fine-tuned. Fine-tuned open-weight models perform best, with a fine-tuned Llama 3.3 70B surpassing the previous best known Exact Match score.

entry.title: Finding and reducing coding agents' habit of accepting choices that skip some requirements
entry.summary: Eliciting and Mitigating Specification Satisficing in Coding Agents arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies specification satisficing, where coding agents pick an implementation that fails a task requirement for reasons they find acceptable. The authors propose SatisFix, which makes the agent report its choices and reasons and then checks each choice against the task description. Tested on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Pro with five LLMs, it raises pass@1 over the base agent and outperforms three self-correction baselines.

entry.title: A framework for learning risk-sensitive individualized treatment rules
entry.summary: Distribution-First Framework for Learning Risk-Sensitive Individualized Treatment Rules arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a distribution-first framework for learning individualized treatment rules that account for risk. It first estimates treatment-specific conditional outcome distributions, then builds the treatment rule by plug-in evaluation of the chosen criterion, allowing quantiles, CVaR, and cumulative prospect theory to be compared in one pipeline. The authors give theoretical results on error propagation and regret bounds, and report that the framework outperforms criterion-specific methods in several settings. It is also evaluated on the ACTG175 HIV clinical trial.

entry.title: SMIC: Shared multiscale input-reference conditioning across Transformer layers for language inference
entry.summary: SMIC: Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning across Transformer Layers for Natural Language Inference arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes SMIC, a method that builds one input-dependent multiscale reference and reuses it across all Transformer layers, with each layer injecting its own transformed conditioning feature before attention. Trained from scratch, the TCT-SMIC variant achieved the highest ten-seed mean accuracy on all three ANLI rounds, and ablations support the method's contribution. The authors also report lower attention redistribution and smaller accuracy changes under perturbation tests, and derive a finite-sample bound on subset-mass redistribution.

entry.title: FlowIR: Depth-Driven Rectified Flow for Infrared Super-Resolution
entry.summary: FlowIR: Depth-driven Rectified Flow for Resolving Thermal Ambiguity in Infrared Super-Resolution arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses the problem that multiple heat sources in low-resolution infrared images often blur together into overlapping responses. It proposes FlowIR, which injects pseudo-3D depth cues into the generation process using depth-guided 3D convolutions and cluster-wise inter-attention to separate objects and reduce cross-source feature mixing. A Thermal-Geometry Consistency Loss enforces geometric alignment during refinement. Built on a lightweight rectified flow backbone, FlowIR restores infrared images in only a few steps, producing sharply separated and geometrically faithful high-resolution results.

entry.title: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Causal Reasoning Research
entry.summary: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Research on Causal Reasoning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper presents Causals, an open knowledge graph designed to support research on causal reasoning. Its initial release, built from news reports, contains 369,184 nodes and 1,272,418 edges linking events, organizations, commodities, and financial instruments. Structural relationships, observations, and attributed causal claims are kept distinct and linked to their source records. The resource is intended for studying how language models retrieve relevant context and apply mechanisms to specific events, and it is available under CC BY 4.0.

entry.title: Rectified Looped Transformer: a feedback method that stabilizes repeated-block language models
entry.summary: Rectified Looped Transformer arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes the Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT), which repeatedly applies a shared Transformer block and forms each loop's next input by linearly interpolating between the current state and its prediction. The authors argue that this interpolation keeps hidden-state magnitudes bounded across loops and reduces worst-case perturbation amplification. In language modeling experiments at matched training and inference depths, RLT achieves lower perplexity than a standard looped Transformer and is more robust to input perturbations and inference-depth variance. It does so without extra trainable parameters or additional recurrent block evaluations.

entry.title: Label-efficient detection of whether claims are supported by a source document
entry.summary: Label-Efficient Document-Grounded Factuality Detection via Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework for checking whether claims generated by large language models are supported by a given document. It turns a small labeled set into relational training pairs, using paraphrased views of the same document-claim instance as positives and opposite-label examples from the same document as negatives, with quantile-aware semi-hard negative mining. At inference, it needs only one encoder-classifier forward pass. On the 11-task LLM-AggreFact benchmark, CPIL using 2-3% of the labeled pool outperforms the compared compact detectors and two vanilla LLM references in macro-F1.

entry.title: Study of how multilingual speech recognisers transfer to unseen low-resource languages
entry.summary: Low Language Transfer Speech-to-Text arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper examines how much multilingual speech-to-text models can carry over to low-resource languages they were never trained on when fine-tuned on limited data. The authors evaluate 28 open multilingual models on Low-Language-TTS, covering 50 low-resource languages in 11 writing systems, and fine-tune 24 of them on at most 1,000 clips per language. Fine-tuning substantially lowers character error rates, and the paper also reports effects of adapters, training epochs, data quantity, and forgetting of known languages.

entry.title: Reconstructing Dynamic Scenes While Removing Distractors in 4D Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: Reconstruct What You Can: Distractor-free 4D Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces ReCan-GS, a 4D Gaussian Splatting framework for reconstructing dynamic scenes from casual video. It computes a Jacobian-based deformation-sensitivity score from the learned deformation field to separate dynamic Core Gaussians from per-view Distractor Gaussians, or to prune sensitive Core Gaussians. The method removes spatial occluders, photometric artifacts, and evolving smoke or fog without masks, pretrained segmenters, or medium-specific supervision. Experiments on synthetic and real dynamic scenes and synthetic smoke/fog scenes are reported.

entry.title: Few-shot cross-subject neural-image retrieval with stimulus-anchored bias calibration
entry.summary: Few-Shot Cross-Subject Neural--Image Retrieval via Stimulus-Anchored Latent Bias Calibration arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses cross-subject retrieval between neural responses and images, proposing Stimulus-Anchored Latent Bias Calibration (SA-LBC). It estimates a target subject's representation shift by averaging residuals against same-stimulus source-population anchors, then shrinks the correction using source-derived uncertainty. On THINGS-EEG2 under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, SA-LBC raises mean reciprocal rank for the Attention–CLIP ViT-B/32 configuration from 0.1867 to 0.2013 with two calibration samples and 0.2336 with sixteen. The authors note that retrieval gains depend on the representation, and that lower shift-estimation error does not guarantee better retrieval.

entry.title: HybridCT: Machine-learning-accelerated 3D cloud tomography for climate-relevant observations
entry.summary: HybridCT: ML Accelerated Tomography for Climate Relevant 3D Cloud Observations arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Low-level clouds are a major source of uncertainty in climate predictions, partly due to a lack of detailed 3D measurements of their internal structure. This paper presents HybridCT, a machine-learning-accelerated tomographic method that recovers 3D cloud extinction directly from passive multi-angle observations. It reconstructs extinction with an RMSE of 13.3 km⁻¹ in 3.5 seconds, compared with 22.7 km⁻¹ in about 30 minutes for the physics-based AT3D framework, a speedup of over 500 times.

entry.title: Can a Vision-Language-Action Model Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Navigation
entry.summary: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Navigation agents call a vision-language-action (VLA) model through a large language model planner, which adds cost and delay to every episode. This paper distills successful agent experience into the VLA itself rather than the planner, so the VLA can navigate alone at test time. The proposed H2E method converts agent sessions into VLA training data, masks the loss on steps that move away from the goal, and labels visited states within 1 m of the goal as stops. On all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%.

entry.title: ATune: Unsupervised Photo Retouching via Image-Editor Controls
entry.summary: ATune: Unsupervised Photo Retouching Through Image-Editor Controls arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents ATune, a photo retouching model trained without expert-edited pairs, using degraded versions of millions of good photographs instead. It learns target values for 13 measurable attributes such as brightness, contrast and sharpness, then searches the sliders of an existing photo editor to reach them. Each edit is a readable list of slider values. In a user study with 157 raters, its edits were preferred over some rival outputs, and in comparisons against supervised methods raters chose ATune 46.3% of the time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors learn retouching without expert edits by degrading photos into training pairs, outputting readable editor slider values, and report comparisons on FiveK, PPR10K and SPAQ.

entry.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions After Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper applies GRPO reinforcement learning to a 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model supporting English and eight Indic languages, across four training environments, and compares 34 benchmarks before and after training. MATH improves by 36.07 points and most Indic benchmarks improve, but XQuAD-Indic F1 drops 19.32 points as English answers rise from 8.7% to 91.7%. A second run adds an Indic environment with language and repetition rewards, improving passage answering and instruction following while losing ground on reasoning and coding. Several training choices changed together, so individual reward effects cannot be isolated, and script compliance remains unresolved.

entry.title: Disentangled Embedding Optimization: A New Diffusion-Based Method for Dataset Distillation
entry.summary: Disentangled Embedding Optimization for Diffusion-Based Dataset Distillation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses dataset distillation, which compresses large datasets into compact synthetic subsets that still support efficient model training. It notes that existing diffusion-based methods use class-wise cluster prototypes that become entangled near cluster boundaries, producing similar inputs and less diverse synthetic data. The proposed Disentangled Embedding Optimization (DEO) replaces static clustering with trainable embeddings that match the Gaussian statistics of the original data, plus a diversity regularizer that improves separation among them. Experiments reportedly yield more diverse and representative distilled data than cluster-based diffusion methods across multiple datasets.

entry.title: We Are What We Remember: Memory Driven by Mental States for Long-Term Character Dialogue
entry.summary: We Are What We Remember: Mental-State-Driven Memory for Long-Term Character Dialogue arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper argues that mainstream conversational memory systems rely on semantic similarity and often retrieve topically similar records while missing relationally important experiences. It proposes MindMem, which asynchronously consolidates shared experiences into mental states of the character, the user, and their relationship, and uses a dedicated reasoner to anticipate user needs and recover supporting episodic evidence. On the newly introduced MemReal-Bench, built from month-long real-user interactions, MindMem reports 59.03% SMR and 82.58% DQA; code and dataset are publicly available.

entry.title: GC-MoE on SM120: Fusing Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with Block-Scaled MMA on Consumer Blackwell GPUs
entry.summary: GC-MoE on SM120: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with Warp-Level FP8xFP4 Block-Scaled MMA on Consumer Blackwell arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper addresses the latency of expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts decoding, where token exchange, grouped expert GEMMs, and result combining are serialized. It rebuilds the GC-MoE fused operator for SM120 consumer Blackwell GPUs (such as RTX PRO 5000) connected over PCIe, using warp-level block-scaled MMA and several SM120-specific mechanisms. On 8 RTX PRO 5000 GPUs across 18 decode points, the operator is 1.522x and 1.387x faster than FlashInfer CuTe DSL W4A8 MegaMoE and Cake MegaMoE, respectively, and all numerical checks pass.

entry.title: WorldDraft: Can video models render worlds that code builds?
entry.summary: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It? arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces WorldDraft, a benchmark of 432 paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families, designed to test whether video models can faithfully render scenes constructed by code. It uses a 3×3 factorial design to vary draft granularity and appearance alignment, and evaluates 12 models. The authors find a tension between preserving the world's dynamics and realizing the target visual attributes, and report source leakage of up to 64% when cues conflict. They also propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting method that improves both objectives on frozen video renderers.

entry.title: Generating Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Models
entry.summary: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper asks whether small open language models running on a laptop can turn reviewed examples of Linux kernel driver conversions into Coccinelle semantic patches. The authors propose a guided generation framework that splits examples into change variants, generates and repairs rules using feedback, and uses a compile critic to reject rules whose output does not build. On a pre-registered test set of 122 held-out driver conversions, the framework lets a local model solve about 35 conversions on average, fewer than Spinfer (41) and a frontier LLM agent (66), but with the highest precision. entry.title: SPEM: Scan-Prior Entropy Modeling for LiDAR Point Cloud Compression
entry.summary: SPEM: Scan-Prior Entropy Modeling for LiDAR Point Cloud Compression arXiv · Nov 12, 2026LiDAR point clouds contain spatial patterns caused by the scanning process, which help compress their geometry. SPEM uses these scanning patterns inside the entropy model without converting coordinates to spherical or beam-aligned systems. It introduces a multi-frequency spherical rotary positional encoding and a decoded-memory autoregressive predictor that reuses previously decoded occupancy information. Experiments report state-of-the-art results for both lossy and lossless LiDAR geometry compression.

entry.title: Adaptive fuzzing framework for neuro-symbolic AI systems (NSAI-Fuzz)
entry.summary: One Fuzzer, Many Reasoners: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzing with Reliability-Calibrated and Context-Gated Guidance arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents NSAI-Fuzz, a unified fuzzing framework for neural-symbolic AI systems that searches for reasoning failures. It scores candidate inputs using five risk signals and adapts their weights with Reliability-Calibrated Weighting and Contextual Signal Gating. Experiments on four systems and four reasoning tasks report higher failure discovery than the strongest neural-fuzzing baseline.

entry.title: Converting multi-agent communication into token-level credit via on-policy self-distillation
entry.summary: Turning Multi-Agent Communication into Token-Level Credit with On Policy Self Distillation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes OPSD4MAS, which uses On Policy Self Distillation to turn future communication in LLM multi-agent systems into fine-grained token-level credit. An external model extracts facts and filters them coarsely, then a leave-one-out step filters target-token influence against agent-wise outcome advantages. The token-level credit is combined with GRPO through a linearly annealed joint objective. The authors report up to 20.00 percentage-point gains in mathematical pass@4 over GRPO.

entry.title: A broad test of machine learning and deep learning methods for judging whether Amazon reviews are positive, neutral, or negative
entry.summary: An Extensive Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Sentiment Analysis: Insights from Amazon Customer Reviews arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper compares five traditional machine learning classifiers and six deep learning models for sorting 568,454 Amazon Fine Food Reviews into three sentiment classes. The models are tested on the original imbalanced data and on a balanced oversampled set, using accuracy, F1-score and training time. On the balanced set, Random Forest with Bag-of-Words features reached 99% accuracy, and the Attention model reached 98.7%.

entry.title: When Can an Interpretability Claim Be Trusted? Stability and Certification of Feature Measures
entry.summary: When can an interpretability claim be trusted? Stability and certification of feature dimensionality, ridge leverage and the feature recovery rate arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines the stability of two common interpretability measurements, feature dimensionality and feature recovery rate with a cosine threshold, using toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth. It replaces feature dimensionality with a ridge-regularized version that has proven stability bounds, and proposes certificates for whether a recovered feature claim survives changes to a dictionary. The certificates hold under small perturbations but are not informative across independently trained dictionaries, where whether a feature counts as recovered changed with training seed for 55 percent of features.

entry.title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Detecting and Explaining Context-Dependent Anomalies in Tables
entry.summary: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes Flow-CAD, a framework that uses Flow Matching to detect contextual anomalies, meaning table rows whose values are unexpected given their context. It learns a single global, amortized conditional generative model of behavior conditioned on context, and scores anomalies with a scale-normalized, truncated residual energy that also supports feature-wise attribution. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets against 13 competitors show Flow-CAD achieves the best average rank on PR AUC, ROC AUC, and P@n.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Safety Alignment for LLMs Guided by Interpretable Features
entry.summary: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes Less is Safer (LIS), a compact safety alignment dataset of 2.4K samples built by selecting prompts with Sparse Autoencoder activations and generating harmless but over-refusal-triggering prompts through multi-agent adversarial synthesis. LIS outperforms much larger datasets such as TRIDENT-Core, TRIDENT-Edge, and WildJailbreak overall across four safety and five over-refusal benchmarks. Ablation experiments indicate that safety data or over-refusal data alone does not achieve optimal results.

entry.title: Same-state pairs make a JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis vacuous
entry.summary: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines the JEPA-based proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which relies on a spectral gap assumption. It shows that under same-state positive pairs the induced world kernel becomes the identity, so the uniqueness claim has no content when k is less than d_z minus 1. The paper also retains a gap-free lower bound on alignment error and describes how paired samples, component semantics, and value anchors fix the canonical frame.

entry.title: Stacking More Levels: Toward General, Human-Like Mario Play
entry.summary: Stack more levels: how to get general and human-like Mario playing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies whether model-free PPO agents trained on Super Mario Bros. levels can win unseen levels. The authors train agents on growing sets of procedurally generated levels and test them on 1000 held-out levels. They then shape the policies into runner, killer, and collector styles and fine-tune them with DRAIL using human gameplay demonstrations, finding that more training levels generally help and fine-tuning increases action-level human-likeness.

entry.title: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance
entry.summary: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces a Society-Centered AI Governance Framework for judging whether a jurisdiction's AI policy instruments let a person get notice of AI influence, challenge a decision, and see it corrected. The authors test it in North Carolina through interviews with nine AI Leadership Council members and a provision-level reading of 49 AI governance documents from 19 states. They find that the state's own AI systems follow visibility-first governance, with notice as an agency duty and AI-specific challenge and correction still advisory.

entry.title: Self-supervised attention-based virtual metrology for predicting CMP material removal rate
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes GREP, a self-supervised, attention-based framework for predicting material removal rate (MRR) in chemical mechanical planarization (CMP). It learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, then applies supervised fine-tuning to estimate MRR. On the PHM 2016 CMP dataset, GREP performs competitively with limited labeled data and achieves a 17.0% RMSE reduction in the final temporal interval.

entry.title: Edge sampling method that uses node features to approximate one-step graph Laplacian messages in graph neural networks
entry.summary: Feature-Aware Edge Sampling for Approximate One-Step Laplacian Propagation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how to approximate one-step combinatorial Laplacian messages in graph neural networks by sampling edges. It proposes a spanning-tree-based hybrid sampler that combines feature-conditioned message scores with effective-resistance leverage scores. The authors derive the expected one-step message error and the optimal sampling probabilities for a given expected edge budget. Preliminary experiments on synthetic community graphs show that message error decreases and classification accuracy rises slightly as the budget grows, with the hybrid sampler performing between optimal selection and uniform random sampling.

entry.title: Generative AI models that track particle motion in 3D fluid flows across frames
entry.summary: Generative AI models for exploring diffusion dynamics from multi-frame particle tracking arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper presents DiffTR-Flow3D, a diffusion-based model that estimates fluid flow motion from three-dimensional particle recordings using a stochastic diffusion process. It conditions the process on both global and local particle dynamics and uses historical particle trajectories to improve estimates. Experiments with numerical simulations and real-world measurements report higher displacement estimation accuracy than learning-based flow estimators and better long-term tracking when integrated into particle tracking pipelines.

entry.title: GOOSELoc: A multimodal dataset for locating ground cameras against aerial maps in off-road terrain
entry.summary: GOOSELoc: A Multimodal Benchmark for Ground-to-Aerial Localization in Unstructured Off-Road Terrain arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces GOOSELoc, a benchmark for localizing ground-level sensors against aerial imagery in unstructured environments such as forests, fields, and rural tracks. It contains 9,356 scenes recorded in all four seasons around Munich, pairing aerial orthophotos with surround-view RGB images and 3D LiDAR point clouds. Four existing cross-view localization methods, fine-tuned on the data, perform substantially worse in off-road settings. The authors propose a multimodal baseline combining surround-view imagery and LiDAR geometry, which improves localization performance.

entry.title: Calibrated Early Stopping with Bounded Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
entry.summary: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies when to stop best-first graph traversal in constrained k-nearest-neighbor vector search, seeking the cheapest stopping rule whose answer is exact with probability at least 1-ε. The proposed method, CaST, builds monotone staircase stopping rules via a linear program solved with Lagrangian duality and calibrates them with fixed-sequence binomial tests. On two datasets of one million items each, CaST costs at most 1.132 times the class optimum and runs faster than other calibrated rules at a common risk target.

entry.title: Spotting Spam SMS Using Transformer Models and Message Timing
entry.summary: Temporal Context-Aware Spam Detection Using Transformer-Based NLP Models arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies outbound SMS spam detection at the carrier level, aiming to predict at send time whether a carrier will flag a message as spam. Using a production database of 43,741 messages with timestamps and delivery statuses, it compares text-only models such as TF-IDF with logistic regression and DeBERTa-v3-base. It also reports a DistilBERT model that adds inter-message temporal features, and proposes TemporalBertSpam, which encodes each sender's message history with a causal Transformer.

entry.title: Split-and-scale: a method to boost latent 3D detail at inference time
entry.summary: Split-and-scale Latent 3D Representations arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper notes that current latent 3D representations struggle to capture fine details of complex objects, and that increasing latent capacity during training is costly. It proposes split-and-scale, which applies one pretrained tokenizer to small sub-regions of a scene at inference, giving the same latent capacity to a smaller area to capture more detail. The authors report reconstruction quality competitive with much larger models that exceed single-GPU memory limits, and show the approach can train an autoregressive 3D generator that performs competitively with state-of-the-art baselines.
